WORKLOG task 1, rework round 15. Draw: prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[4,4]; contact-lens claim 4, stand-alone fitting 4.
SCOPE: task 1 claims vision_ext_oon_contacts_claim (owner=user) and vision_ext_refit_member_share; task 0 holds the exam visit, eyeglasses order, contact-lens order and glasses claim.
WORLD: binder on the deadline day (2026-10-01); the new out-of-network claim of 2026-09-12 (specialty fitting, medically necessary scleral lenses, backup glasses) received 2026-10-24 without a remark; the stand-alone refit of 2026-10-06 at Lindstrom denied as not eligible. Frozen 2026-10-31.
PROBLEM TREE: root vision_ext_refit_member_share; edge vision_ext_refit_member_share<-vision_ext_oon_contacts_claim "The member share of a stand-alone fitting is fixed only after no contact-lens line of the patient on an out-of-network claim dated within sixty calendar days of the fitting still awaits its first decision.". Refit 67.50: eligibility_binder 225.00, tied_fitting_allowance 127.50, new_wearer_allowance 82.50, fit_cost_rule 90.00; baseline 225.00. Multi-source: new_wearer_allowance, fit_cost_rule. DECOY / ABSENT-RECORD PROBES (round 8 re-run, contact-lens claim rows re-run in round 9 on a scratch copy; every LATEST / first-match / XLATEST read: reversed, prior-period, later-period, second record, absent): [reimbursed contacts reversed (X tie reversal read)] refit_member_share: 67.5 -> 187.5; [contacts 75 days before the refit (X tie window)] refit_member_share: 67.5 -> 187.5; [earlier paid fitting under Lindstrom (X returning)] refit_member_share: 67.5 -> 82.5; [earlier paid fitting under Lindstrom reversed (X new-wearer reversal read)] refit_member_share: 67.5 -> 67.5; [contacts elective (C contact basis: elective tier)] oon_contacts_claim: 310.0 -> 205.0; [paid lens 2026-09-05 same period (C contact basis: outside tier; claim frame on its own benefit)] oon_contacts_claim: 310.0 -> 70.0; [paid frame 2026-09-05 same period (C contact basis: outside tier; claim lens on its own benefit)] oon_contacts_claim: 310.0 -> 35.0; [paid lens 2026-09-05 reversed alone on its date (C contact basis reversal read)] oon_contacts_claim: 310.0 -> 310.0; [paid lens 2025-11-05 prior period (C contact basis decoy)] oon_contacts_claim: 310.0 -> 310.0; [paid contacts 2026-09-02 same period (C in-lieu: contacts-held tier)] oon_contacts_claim: 310.0 -> 0.0; [paid contacts 2025-10-02 prior period (C in-lieu decoy)] oon_contacts_claim: 310.0 -> 310.0; [claim without backup glasses (C in-lieu: contacts-only tier)] oon_contacts_claim: 310.0 -> 310.0; [standard fitting (C fitting tier)] oon_contacts_claim: 310.0 -> 240.0; [claim without fitting line (C fitting tier none)] oon_contacts_claim: 310.0 -> 210.0; [plan Essential 100 (C on another in-scope plan)] oon_contacts_claim: 310.0 -> 310.0; [round 11: routine exam line on the refit claim (fitting belongs to the exam visit)] refit_member_share: 67.5 -> 0.0; [round 11: plan Exam Plus, refit at Lindstrom (not covered, in network)] refit_member_share: 67.5 -> 157.5.

STANDARD SOLUTION: verify; read plan, claims, the Lindstrom agreement, account and ledger; Nora files V73-260912-5233 for 310.00 with lens and frame remarks DENIED_CONTACTS_IN_LIEU; the refit 67.50.
ROUND 8 (revision_7 items K1, K2, K3, K4, K6). K1: every sentence that reads a latest service standing PAID or PAID_OON_REIMBURSEMENT (exam visit new-patient test; eyeglasses exam credit; contact-lens order additional-pair frame, fitting tie and new-wearer test; stand-alone fitting tie and new-wearer test; the in-lieu test of the eyeglasses, contact-lens order and both claim rules) now states the reversal rule the compute applies: when that latest one is the only such service on its date and has been reversed there is none and no earlier one is looked at, while of several on that date a reversal of one leaves the date standing; the new-wearer sentences name the standard and specialty fittings read each on its own, as computed. Task 0's reversed duplicate exam V73-261204-4409 therefore leaves Ivy a new patient in the rule words and in the compute alike. K2: the fitting ladders carry the values the record can take: exam visit = routine exam with a specialty fitting line / with a standard fitting line / without a fitting line (0.00); both out-of-network claim rules = specialty fitting line / standard fitting line / no fitting line (0.00); the baselines stay the standard sentences (every exam-visit line at exam_fee_private; a fitting out of network at oon_exam_reimbursement). K3: see DEPARTURES (1). K4: one definition of the benefit period (the twelve months from each year's benefit_period_start_mmdd), stated once in the in-lieu sentence; the compute compares period indexes counted from the reset day (no month windows back from the decision day remain); the auditor's probe (reset day 12-15, paid contacts 2026-12-10) leaves the eyeglasses order at its gold (DECOY table). K6: the contact-lens order's fitting ties first to the order's own contact-lens line when the same decision settles it under the contacts benefit (contacts benefit on the plan, contacts frequency available, no spectacle-lens or frame service counted in the order's benefit period), otherwise to the latest paid or reimbursed contact lenses within the tie window (DECOY table: without the 2027 lens order the own elective lenses tie their fitting). The scored writes, owners, arguments and order are unchanged in both tasks.
ROUND 9 (revision_8 items L1, L2). L1: see DEPARTURES (1): the contact-lens claim now carries eligibility_binder, oon_fitting_schedule, contacts_basis and oon_contacts_in_lieu, every tier reachable on the plans that carry a contacts benefit and distinct in outcome (DECOY table: elective tier, glasses-already-counted tier by a paid lens and by a paid frame, contacts-already-counted tier, contacts-only claim). L2: task 0's closure states the recomputed load of the edge contact-lens order <- eyeglasses order (120.00: without the eyeglasses decision the order's own elective contact lenses are covered and tie its fitting), and the SKIPS and reversed-order figures are restated the same way. The scored writes, owners, arguments and order are unchanged in both tasks.
ROUND 11 (render pre-scan render_r1 items 1-7; no scored value, factor figure or world row moved). (1) The assembly sentences of the contact-lens order and the stand-alone fitting are generic: every discount part that applies is added into one rate taken once off the retail charge, every fitting allowance that applies is added into one combined fitting allowance, and the fitting share is taken as the fitting sentences state; no factor-only quantity is named there. (2) The contact-lens order defines an outside-benefit discount rate (materials_discount_pct) for contact lenses bought outside the benefit for any reason (no benefit on the plan, frequency, in lieu); the additional-pair part adds to that rate, a quantity the base sentences define, and the compute applies it in every outside case. (3) Both member-claim rules state that a fitting line follows its claim's contact-lens line (no reimbursement for the fitting when the contact lenses receive none, same remark). (4) The exam visit states its out-of-network fitting amount (oon_exam_reimbursement, whatever the kind) in its own standard sentence, also in the computation baseline; fitting_type_fee now owns only the participating schedule. (5) Lines belong to exactly one rule: a routine exam line to the exam visit, a fitting to the contact-lens order when its claim carries contact lenses, else to the exam visit when its claim carries a routine exam line, else to the stand-alone fitting; contact lenses to the contact-lens order; spectacle lenses and frames to the eyeglasses order. Each selection sentence now states the compute's precedence (independent practice, then retail chain, then the not-eligible lines; specialty before standard for fittings); the exam visit takes the fitting only on a claim without contact lenses; the stand-alone fitting settles nothing (0.00) when the claim it looks at carries a routine exam or contact-lens line; the contact-lens order counts open spectacle-lens or frame lines of its own claim as glasses (the eyeglasses order of the same claim settled first), so a mixed claim has one outcome in either decision order. The four agent tools now record only the lines their rule owns (the member tools still record every line of the new out-of-network claim); every task claim carries the lines of one rule only, so replay is unchanged. (6) The stand-alone fitting states the not-covered case first (participating: discounted charge; out of network: nothing reimbursed) and then the covered out-of-network reimbursement, as the compute now applies them. (7) Every eligibility sentence and binder ladder says the latest binder payment is read (its return, amount and date), as the compute reads it. Sweep of the same classes over all six rules: factor independence and quote sweep re-run (checks bad = 0); no other rule assembles a factor-only quantity or gates one factor through another.
ROUND 12 (render pre-scan render_r2 items R2-1, R2-2; text and attribution only, compute, worlds and every figure unchanged). R2-1: both member-claim rules carry the sentence that a fitting line follows its claim's contact-lens line in their computation baseline too, attributed to the assembly (result) instead of the in-lieu factor. R2-2: the contact-lens order's sentence defining the outside-benefit discount rate (materials_discount_pct percent) sits in its computation baseline, just before the assembly sentence, attributed to the assembly. Sweep of all six rules: every quantity a computation baseline uses is defined there, and every behaviour of the assembly is stated there and attributed to it: the exam visit's out-of-network fitting sentence now belongs to its assembly; the stand-alone fitting's rule for a claim that also carries an exam or contact-lens line is its own sentence before the assembly, attributed to it; the eyeglasses order and the member claims' other assembly behaviours were already stated in their baselines.
ROUND 13 (coordinator finding on the published KB: composed denied-line strings had no verbatim source). Every decision and filing tool now takes one remark argument per line kind it records (exam visit: exam_remark, fitting_remark; eyeglasses order: lenses_remark, frame_remark; contact-lens order: fitting_remark, contact_lenses_remark; stand-alone fitting: fitting_remark; both member filings: all five), each a single remark code from the listed set (DENIED_FREQUENCY, DENIED_CONTACTS_IN_LIEU, DENIED_NOT_COVERED, DENIED_NOT_ELIGIBLE, DENIED_TIMELY_FILING) or empty for an absent or paid line; tool bodies and their writes are otherwise unchanged, so every world row the gold leaves is the same. Gold calls carry every remark argument of their tool explicitly; rules and figures unchanged.
ROUND 14 (KB audit S1, S2). S1: the two member-claim rules both claimed V73-261211-4502 because each tested the side with its own amounts (children's frame 90.00 in one, 70.00 in the other). The side test is now one shared receipts-only sentence in both rules (record composition, no rule's pricing), with a compute guard in each rule and a refusal in each member tool; probes: [T0 claim V73-261211-4502 under the glasses claim rule] -> 140.0; [T0 claim V73-261211-4502 under the contact-lens claim rule (not its side: records nothing)] -> 0.0; [T1 claim V73-260912-5233 under the contact-lens claim rule] -> 310.0; [T1 claim V73-260912-5233 under the glasses claim rule (not its side: records nothing)] -> 0.0; [T0: contact-lens filing tried first, then the glasses filing] -> ['Not settled on its contact-lens part: the spectacle-lens and frame receipts of claim V73-2', "{'claim_number': 'V73-261211-4502', 'plan_paid': 140.0, 'lines': {'af4117ae-c131-4efa-a8a2"]; [  then the eyeglasses order] -> 457.0; [T1: glasses filing tried first, then the contact-lens filing] -> ['Not settled on its glasses part: the contact-lens and fitting receipts of claim V73-260912', "{'claim_number': 'V73-260912-5233', 'plan_paid': 310.0, 'lines': {'d4adf765-37cc-4b95-b18c"]; [  then the refit] -> 67.5. No scored value, factor figure or edge load moves (task 0: 140.00 / 457.00 / 262.50 on the glasses side, task 1: 310.00 / 67.50 on the contact-lens side). S2: every provider agreement's credentialing decision date is now its latest recredentialing decision, 36 months before its recredential due date (Kessler 2026-11-01, Iverson 2025-05-01, Lindstrom 2025-05-01); application and effective dates keep the original credentialing.
ROUND 15 (revision_14 item N1; no scored value, factor figure or world row moved). The contact-lens claim rule now prices a child's out-of-network frame exactly as the glasses claim rule does, in its in-lieu comparison and when every line is reimbursed: the same frame-amount sentence (nothing without a frame benefit; oon_child_frame_reimbursement for a patient under child_age_limit_years; oon_frame_reimbursement otherwise), the same compute, stated in its computation baseline and declared in its scoped overwrite; it also states, as the glasses rule does, that lens options are never reimbursed. One comparison of every amount the two rules share (exam, fitting, contact lenses, lenses, frame, options, copays, coverage gates, fitting-follows, side test) is listed in worklog.md; the frame was the only difference. Ivy probes (glasses rule / contact-lens rule): [Ivy V73-261211-4502 as seeded (receipts 590.00 vs 220.00)] 140.0 / 0.0; [Ivy decoy: contact-lens receipt 700.00 (760.00 > 590.00, contact-lens rule)] 0.0 / 140.0; [Ivy decoy at 700.00, patient aged 19 or more (adult frame amount)] 0.0 / 135.0.
ROUND 7 (revision_6 items J1-J3, J10 closed as proposed; J4-J8 struck; coordinator DECISION merging services the way one visit or one order is adjudicated). Policies: exam visit (routine exam and fitting lines of one claim, decide_exam_visit_80d2e33d), eyeglasses order (lens and frame lines of one claim, decide_eyeglasses_order_e7a7f40f), contact-lens order (contact-lens and fitting lines of one claim, decide_contacts_order_55f7002b), stand-alone fitting (decide_contact_fitting_9468302b), and the member's new out-of-network claim settled on its glasses part (file_oon_eyeglass_claim_2513bc70) or on its contact-lens part (file_oon_contact_lens_claim_04f2b50e). The agent rules also reprocess an out-of-network claim already filed and denied as not eligible, under the out-of-network tier of each channel ladder; the member tools record only lines that carry no remark yet. Removed: decide_exam_service_5f5caac3, decide_lens_order_308134ce and the single-service rules they carried.
J1: every real dependency is an edge (task 0: glasses claim <- exam visit; eyeglasses order <- exam visit and <- glasses claim; contact-lens order <- eyeglasses order and <- glasses claim) and the resolution order is total, so no pair is claimed to commute; reversed orders were run (worklog SKIPS). J2: the frequency sentences count from the latest paid or reimbursed service of the kind; a reversal frees the benefit only when it reverses the one paid service on that latest date (several on that date leave it blocked, whatever the row order); this and the current-enrollment scope are declared as a scoped overwrite naming the five sibling rules. J3 (re-stated in round 8 for K4): contacts-in-lieu reads, for each kind of the other side (spectacle lenses, frames, contact lenses), the latest paid or reimbursed service with the reversal rule of the frequency sentence, and counts it when it is dated in the same benefit period as the service settled, a benefit period starting each year on benefit_period_start_mmdd; a latest service in another benefit period counts nothing; declared as a scoped overwrite naming the five sibling rules. J10: the fitting line counts in the contact-lens part of the in-lieu comparison and follows the contact-lens line; a fitting on a claim without contact lenses is reimbursed on its own. J4: the location split of the child copay is gone; one pediatric band remains as a three-tier ladder with the out-of-network tier (no copay out of network) on agent rules that now settle out-of-network lines. J5: no new-wearer discount on contact lenses; new-wearer allowances exist only on fittings. J6: no exam-and-eyewear allowance on out-of-network reimbursement. J7: frequency is the base rule in every computation document, never a factor. J8: no tier exists only on Exam Plus except the children's frame tier for plans without a frame benefit, which the coordinator admitted where it changes the number (on Exam Plus a child's out-of-network frame would otherwise get oon_child_frame_reimbursement).
SPLIT OF THE TWO MEMBER-CLAIM RULES (round 14, KB audit S1): one shared sentence, word for word the same in both rules and computed the same way in both, fixes the side by receipts alone: a claim whose spectacle-lens and frame retail charges together are at least its contact-lens and fitting retail charges together is settled on its glasses part, any other on its contact-lens part; each rule records nothing (0.00) for a claim of the other side and each member tool refuses such a claim, so exactly one rule claims every claim, whatever either rule's amounts. Inside its rule each claim keeps its in-lieu comparison of reimbursed parts at that rule's amounts.
DEPARTURES AND WHY: (1) Rounds 8-9 (K3, L1): the backup glasses' lens-type schedule cannot change the contact-lens claim's number while its contact-lens part is kept (its baseline oon_single_vision_reimbursement is the smallest lens amount), and the refit's tie needs that part kept; a ladder on the certified reason alone has only two values on the plans that carry a contacts benefit (contact_lens_reason is elective or medically_necessary; every plan with a contacts benefit has covered_in_full), and the plan tier for plans without a contacts benefit only selected 0.00 where every other tier is also 0.00 (Exam Plus). Round 9 takes the coordinator's option (a): the claim's in-lieu factor is a genuine three-tier method (a contact-lens service already counted in the benefit period leaves the glasses lines out; a claim with both parts pays the larger; a claim with contact lenses only pays every line), and the test of a spectacle-lens or frame service already counted in the period moves into a contact-lens amount factor, contacts_basis (parameter), with the tiers of the contact-lens order's in_lieu_basis (glasses already counted -> 0.00, the contact-lens line denied in lieu and its fitting following it; otherwise medically necessary -> oon_contacts_medically_necessary_reimbursement; otherwise elective -> oon_contacts_elective_reimbursement). Both factors read the period through the shared latest-service reads; neither reads the other's binding; the comparison and the order (contact-lens settlement first, then contacts-in-lieu) live in the assembly. A plan without a contacts benefit is handled by the claim rule's not-covered sentence (base vision_evt_in_network_benefits / vision_evt_medically_necessary_contacts), never by a factor tier. Options (b) and (c) were not taken: (b) leaves a two-value reason ladder, (c) would re-split the two member-claim rules and move task 0's glasses claim. (1b) Round 8 (K4): the compute language has no date-range aggregate, so a count of every paid service between two reset days cannot be computed exactly for every frozen date; the in-lieu test therefore reads the latest paid or reimbursed service of each kind of the other side, the way vision_msr_last_paid_service and base vision_evt_frequency count contact lenses against the lens and frame benefits, and counts it only in the service's own benefit period from the reset day. (2) The exam visit uses the copay band instead of the evaluation add-on: the add-on is excluded whenever the visit itself bills a fitting (H8 non-duplication), and the visit's fitting is what makes the exam-type fee schedule bite. (3) The decision tools book the claim's one amount on its first undenied line, the other lines carrying no separate amount, because the schema has no claim-level amount field.
TRIGGER RULE (XF-14): tools write only vision_claims rows of vision_exam_claim, vision_lens_claim, vision_frame_claim and vision_contacts_claim; base triggers [] for all four.
FACTOR INDEPENDENCE (XF-1, round 8 re-run): scratch checks8.py closes every factor binding's reads through plain bindings; no factor reaches another factor's binding, no plain binding other than result reads a factor binding, no duplicate binding names: "checks bad = 0".
QUOTE SWEEP (XF-9): every compute_basis value, policy_source and replaced_by is a verbatim substring of its rule (0 misses); each rounding sentence matches the single int(x*100+0.5)/100 around result.
METHOD-SHAPE ALL-PAIRS: eligibility_binder (all six): late (constant) vs binder (benefit formula) vs record (status/date pick) - each pair differs by an operation or input. in-lieu (glasses claim): drop contact side vs drop glasses side vs keep the larger (adds a comparison) vs keep all (adds both sides). in-lieu (contact-lens claim): drop glasses side vs keep the larger (adds a comparison) vs keep all. (contacts_basis on the contact-lens claim is a parameter factor: 0.00 when glasses already count in the period, the fitting following the contact-lens line as the claim rule states; otherwise the medically necessary or the elective out-of-network amount.) in_lieu_basis (contact-lens order): retail less the summed rate vs materials copay constant vs copay plus the part above the allowance. fit_cost_rule (contact-lens order, stand-alone fitting): contracted fee less allowance vs contracted fee alone vs benefit with cap.
user_scenario: You are Nora Lockhart, a graphic designer in Portland who joined Cascade Mutual in August with an individual Cascade Vision Select 150 plan that started September 1; you mailed a check for your first premium that arrived on October 1. You are calling from 5035550186 about one bill: on October 6 Dr. Karin Lindstrom at Lindstrom Eye Associates refitted your specialty contact lenses, and the explanation of benefits says the fitting was not eligible, so the practice billed you the whole charge. You speak calmly and precisely, and you open by asking Cascade to decide that fitting now and tell you what your share of it is. To verify, you give your date of birth, 1991-11-03, and your ZIP code, 97214, when asked; if asked about other vision coverage, you say you have none. You do not know plan rules or amounts and you never suggest any. If the representative explains that you have something to file or settle first, you say you are happy to do your part. When the representative hands you a step to run yourself, you run it with exactly the claim number, amount and line details they give you and read back what it returns. Once the representative tells you your share of the fitting is recorded, you thank them and end the call.
